content.title: Developer Dykstra Determined to Build Housing Development on Cornfield, Fair Share Housing Judge to Decide Sparta's Fate
content.text: SPARTA, NJ – The threat of a development on the cornfield across from North Village is still alive. While Sparta prevailed on all counts in Judge Minkowitz’s court, DDG OPS – Owen Dykstra, is still pushing his plan to build.The next venue for Dykstra/DDG OPS is with Fair Share Housing Judge Allen. By April 30, 2026 a decision has to be made on this remaining issue for Sparta to complete their Housing Element and Fair Share Plan or HEFSP. Dykstra, through DDG OPS LLC is under contract to purchase Awesome Acres LLC, approximately 37 acres of land owned by the Wilson family, for $4.5 million. Frank Barbosa and John Ursin represent DDG OPS LLC. Story continues below newsletter sign upSign Up for FREE Sparta NewsletterGet local news you can trust in your inbox.On September 2, 2025, Dykstra/DDG OPS challenged Sparta’s Fair Share Housing Plan, saying they could build 400 housing units in several four-story buildings with 20% or 80 units to be “set aside” to meet Sparta’s HEFSP. His plan included building an “onsite wastewater treatment facility.” Dykstra/DDG OPS later amended their plan to “a four-story 272-unit family rental project.” Sparta has filed four objections to Dykstra’s challenge: Four-story buildings are out of character with development in Sparta Sensitive environmental concerns are not adequately addressed Sewer capacity may be inadequate Proposed parking is insufficient Sparta Township Attorney Anand Dash said that “while the Township always has and will continue in good faith to honor its duty to provide a reasonable opportunity for affordable housing, developers should heed our Supreme Court’s admonition more than 40 years ago in Mt. Laurel II, that ‘Builders may not be able to build just where they want—our parks, farms, and conservation areas are not a land bank for housing speculators.’” Dash said, “For those developers who fail to heed that warning and instead abuse their rights under the guise of affordable housing, the township will exercise all legal rights to ensure that the interests of its citizenry are protected over the narrow interests of certain developers.”Negotiations between the township and Dykstra/DDG OPS, handled by Fair Share Housing Act Program Judge Thomas Miller, Ret. has not reached a conclusion. Dykstra/DDG OPS's challenge remains open.Sparta continues to refute Dykstra’s challenge. Much of the township’s arguments are laid out in zoning ordinance 25-06 for changes to the PCED zone and the companion resolution 30-page resolution 9-4. Sparta made clear there should be no residential units in that zone for several reasons. Not only is it not in keeping with the character of the town, but residents have expressed concerns about the safety issues that already exist in that area of Route 15 and increased pressure on the schools, police and other infrastructure. Several surveys and meetings with residents to garner input for the new Master Plan have also shown residents value and want to maintain open space.Third AttemptThis is Dykstra’s third attempt to sue his way to building another large development across the street from his North Village. It is his second challenge to Sparta’s HEFSP. Judge Minkowitz upheld Sparta’s zoning change, restricting permitted uses in the Planned Commercial Economic Development or PCED zone to agriculture and recreation. DDG OPS LLC, Awesome Acres LLC and Edward Blevins and Gia Leo as WTTS Real Estate LLC sued to overturn the restrictions put in place in the new ordinance. Sparta successfully argued it was a safety and ecological hazard to allow anything but agriculture and recreation in that zone. In addition to suing and losing over the PCED zoning ordinance, DDG OPS initially filed an “Answer and Challenge” to the number of low-income units Sparta should be required to provide.Judge Miller agreed with Sparta in that first challenge. In his recommendation to Judge Allen in March 2025, Miller said DDG OPS’s complaints should be dismissed for failure to “state with particularity” how Sparta’s calculation is not in compliance with the state’s requirements and included "the challenger’s own calculation of the fair share obligations."These decisions have not discouraged Dykstra/DDG OPS from pursuing their plan to build on the cornfield. Judge Allen will decide if their desire for what Sparta called “urban sprawl” is allowed or if Sparta gets to retain the open space residents desire. Other Challenges to Sparta’s Fair Share Housing Plan.Sparta Township has successfully negotiated with 5 West Shore Trail – Joseph Passalaqua and Jersey Investors Growth Co after settlement conferences on October 2 and December 23, 2025, according to the Affordable Housing Dispute Resolution Program recommendation by Judge Thomas Miller on Feb 5, 2026. Sparta was represented by the township’s fair share housing attorney Steve Warner, planner Catherine Sarmad, and manager James Zepp in those settlement negotiations.
